oewn-00028468-n.learner: the endless flow in which things move from the future, through the present, into the past
examples: Time passes slowly when you are waiting for news.

oewn-15154879-n.learner: the exact point in the day that a clock shows
examples: She looked at the clock to check the time.

oewn-07302920-n.learner: what a person lives through on one particular occasion
examples: We had a wonderful time at the party.

oewn-04998860-n.learner: the rhythm of music, made by dividing it into parts of equal length
examples: The dancers clapped in time with the music.

oewn-15249488-n.learner: the length of time a prisoner has to spend in prison
examples: He did time in the county jail for stealing a car.

oewn-15160774-n.learner: the fourth measurement, added to the three measurements of space, that is needed to fix exactly when and where a physical event happens
examples: In physics, time is treated as a fourth dimension alongside length, width and height.

oewn-15190004-n.learner: the hours between sunrise and sunset, when it is light outside
examples: Owls sleep during the day and hunt at night.

oewn-15161405-n.learner: the hours you are awake, coming again each day, especially the hours you spend working
examples: She had a long day at the office and went straight to bed.

oewn-15182185-n.learner: a day set apart for a special purpose or for marking a special occasion
examples: We gave our mother flowers on Mother's Day.

oewn-14508100-n.learner: a period when you have your chance to do something
examples: Everyone deserves their day in court.

oewn-15233336-n.learner: the time a particular planet, such as Mars, takes to turn once completely on its axis
examples: A day on Jupiter lasts only about ten hours.

oewn-15233129-n.learner: the time the earth takes to turn once completely when measured against a particular star, about four minutes shorter than an ordinary 24-hour day
examples: Measured against the stars, a day is about four minutes shorter than 24 hours.

oewn-00748704-v.learner: to give someone instructions, or to direct them with authority to do something
examples: The teacher told us to sit down and be quiet.
I could tell that she was upset.

oewn-00652006-v.learner: to see or show that one thing is different from another
examples: The twins look so alike that I can't tell them apart.

oewn-01021652-v.learner: to let someone know something firmly, feeling sure and certain that it is true
examples: I tell you, it wasn't me who broke the window!

oewn-00685987-v.learner: to accept that a person, or what they say or write, is telling the truth
examples: Don't believe him; he never tells the truth.

oewn-00686192-v.learner: to have a faith, and follow its set of beliefs as a believer
examples: After hearing the preacher, she too began to believe.

oewn-05715665-n.learner: an understanding of something that you have by instinct
examples: She has a real feeling for colour and design.

oewn-14549784-n.learner: the general mood of a place or situation and the effect it has on people
examples: The old house had a warm, friendly feeling.

oewn-05730374-n.learner: what you sense through your skin when something presses against it
examples: The fabric had a silky feeling under her fingers.

oewn-05798457-n.learner: the word as used in set formal phrases, such as serving 'at the pleasure of' someone
examples: The ministers serve at the pleasure of the king.
He took his pleasure with her and left before dawn.

oewn-84187159-n.learner: a woman who serves in the armed forces, as a member of a military force
examples: The commander ordered her women to hold the bridge.

oewn-10149967-n.learner: a friendly, informal way of speaking of a grown woman
examples: I'm going out with the girls from the office on Friday.

connotation.why: a word for a child used of a grown woman, against plain 'woman'

oewn-02751047-v.learner: to be something extra that is added to something else
examples: The new garden adds to the value of the house.

oewn-02329474-v.learner: to give a certain quality to something
examples: Her quiet humour added charm to the whole evening.

oewn-00951320-v.learner: to work out the total that things come to when they are counted together
examples: When we added the guests from both families, there were over two hundred.

oewn-00594097-v.learner: to think that something is reasonable, or that it is owed to you
examples: After such rudeness, it is only fair to expect an apology.

oewn-00059147-v.learner: to be waiting for your baby to be born
examples: Sam and his wife are expecting again.

oewn-00058790-v.learner: to be pregnant with a baby
examples: She is expecting twins.
